narrative.overview:
A premium, attentive companion in your pocket. The world is a dark, lined wallet interior: deep navy layers, a soft aurora drifting behind them, and glass-edged panels that sit quietly until something is worth your attention. When an answer arrives (the best card, the shekels saved, the one action to take), it is lit in glossy Savings Mint. The concierge is calm by default and confident when it speaks.

Density is phone-first and compact: one centered column, readable at arm's length in a noisy store, built for one thumb. Hebrew leads and the layout is right-to-left at its core, not mirrored after the fact. The concierge also has manners and a little warmth: birthday banners in Celebration Pink, a shimmering headline on the home guide, and a catch-the-shekels coin game while you wait. A small luxury on a free app.

Color comes from the cards themselves. Issuer card art (Max pink, Shufersal red, Rebar green) supplies the vivid color. The chrome around it stays navy so your own cards are the brightest thing in the wallet.
keyCharacteristics: Dark only: deep navy tonal layers over a fixed violet and mint aurora.
Calm panels, glossy answer: flat bordered surfaces, with gloss and glow saved for the primary action, the active chip and savings.
Issuer card art is the color source. UI chrome never borrows brand colors.
One type family (Heebo) for Hebrew and Latin, with mono only for codes and card digits.
Soft, nested rounding from 24px hero shells down to full pills.
Every tap answers instantly: a press-down scale, a spinner, a fade-up entrance. Reduced motion is respected globally.

rules.name: The Mint Means Money Rule
rules.body: Savings Mint marks savings, the winning result and the single primary action in view. If it isn't about saving money or moving forward, it isn't mint.

rules.name: The Cards Bring the Color Rule
rules.body: Issuer brand colors live only on card art and card swatches, where they help people recognize their own cards. Buttons, banners, chips and headings never use them.

rules.name: The Tinted Status Rule
rules.body: Warn, error, success and celebration states use the hue as text, a 10% tint as fill and a 30% tint as border. Never a solid saturated fill.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Heebo everywhere. Monospace appears only for strings a person types or reads out at the register (coupon codes, card digits), set left-to-right inside the RTL flow.

rules.name: The Shekel Figure Rule
rules.body: A computed saving is the loudest number on its card: 1.125rem, 700, in Savings Mint, aligned to the end edge, with a caption beneath.

rules.name: The Start Side Rule
rules.body: Use logical properties (start/end, inline-start/inline-end) for every inset, alignment and icon position. Physical left and right are a bug in an RTL-first app.

rules.name: The Thumb Reach Rule
rules.body: Navigation floats at the bottom inside the safe area, and the main input sits near the top of its screen. On a phone, nothing important lives only in the top corners.

rules.name: The Gloss Is Earned Rule
rules.body: Panels stay flat at rest. Gloss, glow and the shine sweep appear only on the primary action, an active chip, or a savings mark. If everything shines, nothing does.

rules.name: The Nested Radius Rule
rules.body: An inner element never has a larger radius than its container. Step down 24 → 16 → 12 → 8 → full pills only for free-standing tags.

dos: **Do** reserve the glossy mint gradient for the primary action, active chips and savings marks (The Mint Means Money Rule).
**Do** build depth with tone (#161d38 → #222b4d → #2c365c), a 1px #3d4873 border and the 5% white top highlight, before reaching for a shadow.
**Do** draw issuer cards as two-stop gradients with a wordmark, at 1.6:1. Brand colors stay on card art and swatches.
**Do** use logical start/end properties everywhere, and mark LTR islands (codes, digits, English names) locally.
**Do** give every tap immediate feedback: 0.98 press scale, a spinner on loading buttons, and the coin-game waiting screen for long operations.
**Do** enter new content with `fade-up` (0.6s) or `pop-in` (0.35s) on `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1)`, and keep the global reduced-motion override intact.
**Do** use Celebration Pink for special dates and gift cards, Nudge Amber for "spend more" nudges and Alert Coral for errors, all as tinted pills or notices.
donts: **Don't** use issuer brand colors (Max pink, Shufersal red, Rebar green…) on buttons, banners, chips or headings. The app is not affiliated with any issuer.
**Don't** put drop shadows on panels or cards. Only mint fills, the hoisted answer, wallet card art and the floating nav get real depth.
**Don't** use mint for decoration, headings or non-savings emphasis.
**Don't** introduce a second typeface. Monospace is only for codes and card digits.
**Don't** use physical left/right for layout or icon placement.
**Don't** ship a light surface or light-only component. The app is dark-only until a light theme is designed as a whole.
**Don't** use solid saturated fills for status. Use the hue as text over a 10% tint.
